text:
Alex: Heads-up — getting a cluster of 502s from edge in eu-west1 starting ~00:12 UTC, looks correlated with IPv6 clients. SLO alert fired.
Priya: Any pattern in source IPs or UA? can you paste one of the raw request logs?
Alex: pasted a sample log: `client_ip=2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334 route=edge/model-serving status=502 backend=unreachable`
Mateo: Hmm, logs also show a lot of connections coming from our NAT64 pool addresses (64:ff9b::/96) -> indicates clients tried IPv6, we fell back to NAT64 for egress to some internal telemetry backend. :thinking:
ops-bot: deploy 1845.3 rolled at 2026-03-18T00:05:00Z — config change: edge-lb dualstack=ENABLED
Grace: We flipped LB dual-stack flag last night to test dualstack support. I think the LB started advertising AAAA for the edge hostname but our target groups didn't have IPv6 targets registered.
Jun: If LB advertises AAAA but no healthy IPv6 targets, some resolvers will still prefer AAAA and then traffic can hit a translation path/NAT gateway fallback — that can cause ephemeral port contention and backend connections to stall.
Alex: I ran `dig +short AAAA edge.redwood.example.net` and got the LB AAAA. `curl -6 -v https://edge.redwood.example.net/api/v1/health` -> TLS handshake times out.
Priya: Can we verify target group health over IPv6? Mateo, can you check `curl -6` from one of the edge nodes or run `ss -nat | grep 64:ff9b` to see translation sockets?
Mateo: Ran quick tcpdump on the host, snippet:
```
02:14:35.123 IP6 2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334 > 2a01:4f8:xxxx::1: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1232,sackOK,TS val 1234], length 0
02:14:35.124 IP 64.255.0.12.10500 > 10.0.13.22.443: Flags [S], seq 0, ...
```
Shows SYNs arriving as v6, being translated to IPv4 to talk to the backend, but the backend closed or never accepted -> SYN retransmits and then 502 at the LB.
Grace: Also seeing a cost blip in nw-egress:bytes in billing — looks like lots of cross-AZ egress because the NAT64 path forced traffic through a central NAT gateway in a different AZ.
Jun: Short-term mitigation options:
- Disable AAAA advertisement on the LB (turn dualstack OFF) for eu-west1 edge host — simple rollback.
- Add IPv6-enabled targets to target group (requires nodes with IPv6 interfaces or enable IPv6 on nodepool) — more work.
- Increase NAT ephemeral ports / open more gateway capacity to avoid port exhaustion (works around symptoms).
Priya: Quick test we can do now: disable AAAA on one LB zone as a canary and watch 502 rate. Grace, can you flip on one AZ only?
Grace: Yep I can toggle advertise_aaaa for zone-a. Doing it now.
ops-bot: change: lb/edge-eu-west1 zone-a advertise_aaaa=false by Grace at 2026-03-18T00:22:10Z
Alex: After disabling AAAA in zone-a, 502s dropped ~70% for traffic routed to that zone. Still seeing a few in other zones.
Mateo: We should patch the healthcheck to explicitly probe over IPv6 when dualstack enabled so LB won't mark v6 targets healthy unless they actually are.
Jun: Agreed. k8s service short-term annotation to force single-stack IPv4 for the service (if we don't have v6 nodepool ready):
```
kubectl annotate svc edge-proxy network.alpha.kubernetes.io/ip-family=IPv4 --overwrite
kubectl patch svc edge-proxy -p '{"spec":{"ipFamilyPolicy":"SingleStack","ipFamilies":["IPv4"]}}'
```
Note: test in canary ns first.
Priya: Can we also add a telemetry metric for "translation hops" (client-ip is ipv6 && backend-ip is ipv4) so we can alert when NAT64 usage spikes? That would have caught this earlier.
Grace: Logged infra ticket INFRA-1927 to add that metric and to plan ipv6 nodepool rollout for edge. Also adding runbook steps for rollback of advertise_aaaa.
Alex: Action items for now: (1) keep AAAA disabled in zone-a canary, (2) patch service to singlestack where needed, (3) add NAT64/translation metric, (4) scope full dualstack rollout (ipv6-capable nodes + healthchecks). I'll own the canary monitoring.
Priya: Thanks — add me to INFRA-1927 for tracking. :thumbsup:
Mateo: I also want to investigate whether our internal metrics ingestion endpoints accept v6 natively; if not we should avoid translation for that traffic to preserve telemetry.
Jun: Long term: proper dualstack means LB advertises AAAA only when targets are actually reachable over v6 and healthchecks succeed; we need gating in the control plane for that. Filing RFC.
Alex: Good call. For now the rollback reduced customer impact — will follow up with postmortem if rates don't stabilize.
